title: Apply for an agent services account
text:
Who this affects

 If you deal with HMRC about someone else’s tax affairs and get paid for it, you may need to register as a tax adviser with HMRC.

 The requirement to register is being introduced in stages and depends on your circumstances. Check when you need to register with HMRC as a tax adviser .

 There’s a different way to apply for an agent services account if you’re not based in the UK .

 What you’ll need

 You’ll need:

 • your business Government Gateway user ID and password (you can create these on the sign-in page if you do not have them)

 • your personal Government Gateway user ID and password (if you are a sole trader)

 • the Unique Taxpayer Reference ( UTR ) for your firm

 • the postcode linked to your UTR 

 • your company registration number (if you have one)

 • your VAT registration number (if you have one)

 • the name of your anti-money laundering supervisory body , and proof you are supervised

 • the names and contact details of relevant people in your business

 HMRC will reject your application for an agent services account if you’ve applied for anti-money laundering supervision with HMRC or another supervisory body but your application has not yet been approved. You must have approved anti-money laundering supervision in place before you apply.

 During the application process, the service will give you a link.
Share this with any relevant individuals in your business so they can sign in and add their details.
They must use their own Government Gateway user ID, not the business ID.

 Apply for an agent services account

 Sign in using the Government Gateway user ID and password for the business applying for the account.

 If you do not have sign-in details, you can create them on the sign-in page.

 You have 72 days from starting your application to complete and submit it. If you do not submit your application within this time:

 • your application will expire

 • you will need to start a new application

 Apply now 

 Online services may be slow during busy times. Check if there are any problems with this service .

 After you apply for an account

 How long the process takes

 We’ll check your details after you apply.

 This can take longer if we need more information from you or need to carry out extra checks in line with HMRC’s conditions for registering as a tax adviser .

 You can check the progress of an existing application. 

 What you can do now

 Once you have set up an agent services account, you can use HMRC’s online services and interact with HMRC on behalf of your clients.

 If your business is required to register with HMRC as a tax adviser, you may be asked for your Agent Reference Number ( ARN ) when you contact HMRC to discuss your client’s tax affairs. This includes businesses that already have Self Assessment or Corporation Tax agent codes.

 Your ARN confirms that you, or the business you represent, are registered with HMRC as a tax adviser. The ARN is not a security credential, and does not, on its own, confirm your identity or that you are authorised to act for a client. ARN checks are in addition to existing security, identity and client-authorisation checks.

 Anyone contacting HMRC on behalf of your business about a client’s tax affairs should have your business’s ARN ready. If you cannot provide your ARN when asked, HMRC may be unable to discuss your client’s tax affairs with you.

 You can find your ARN in your agent services account. The ARN is an 11-character reference made up of four letters, including ‘ ARN ’ followed by 7 numbers, for example: XARN1234567.

 You must always meet the registration requirements, no matter how your business works with HMRC.

 If you are a paid agent submitting Income Tax or PAYE repayment claims, and you want the repayment paid to you, check the guidance on receiving repayments on behalf of others .

 If your business uses services in the agent services account, you should:

 • sign in and ask your clients to authorise your request authorisation from your clients 

 • create a Government Gateway user ID for each member of staff 

 • set permissions to control their access to services and clients

 Standards for agents

 You must not use your agent services account to suggest that:

 • HMRC endorses you as a tax adviser

 • you are part of HMRC

 • you act on behalf of HMRC

 HMRC does not endorse individual businesses or tax agents.
changeNote: The timeframe for completing an application has been added to the section ‘Apply for an agent services account’. The ‘What you can do now’ section has been updated to advise that agents must provide their Agents Reference Number (ARN) when contacting HMRC.
